# ROOTS-AI™ — M3 closure register

Everything ROOTS has raised, in one place, with what was done, what proves it, and what is
still needed. Prepared in response to the review of 29 September 2026, section F.

**Generated by** `npm run evidence:closure`. Every document cited below is checked to exist,
and the run fails if one does not, so a reference cannot rot into a decoration.

## Where things stand

| State | Items | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| **Closed** | 9 | Done and evidenced. Nothing needed from ROOTS. |
| **Delivered — awaiting ROOTS** | 8 | Done and evidenced. A ROOTS decision closes it. |
| **Blocked on ROOTS or access** | 6 | Everything we can do is done. The rest needs access, devices or a decision we cannot make. |
| **Open** | 0 | Not started, with the reason given. |
| Total | 23 | |

The distinction that matters: **nothing below is waiting on us**. The items that are not closed
are waiting on a decision, a credential or a device, and each says which.

## What cannot be evidenced from a repository

Stated so this register is never read as a completeness claim. Each has a plan; none has a
result, and none can have one from here.

| Requirement | What it needs |
|---|---|
| §13.1 suite 11 — backup and restore | Production credentials and a restore target |
| §12 conditioned metrics | Agreed conditions and a staging environment |
| §12.1 browser matrix | The device and browser matrix |
| Screen-reader verification | Assistive technology on real devices |
| Availability 99.9% monthly | A production month with monitoring |
| Database probes on the client project | We never query the client database; the suites are supplied to be run there |

## Not in our record

We work from the review text as we received it. These identifiers in ROOTS' numbering have no
entry above:

`Item 4`, `Item 5`, `Item 6`, `Item 8`, `Item 9`, `D1`, `D3`, `D6`.

That may be because they were addressed under another heading, because they carried no action,
or because we did not receive them. **If any of them requires something of us, naming it will
get it an entry.** A register that quietly omits what it does not know is worse than one that
says so.
